utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody in court today. And Mr. Registrar would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-83-T, Prosecutor versus Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could we have the appearances, please, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours, counsel and everyone in and around the courtroom. For the Prosecution, Daryl Mundis and Matthias Neuner, assisted by our case manager, Alma Imamovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to my learned friends from the OTP, to all those in and around the courtroom. My name is Vasvija Vidovic and together with Mr. Nicholas Robson, I represent Mr. Delic. With us we have our assistants Lana Deljkic and Lejla Gluhic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Vidovic. Can we just hold on please. We're having a problem. It looks like we are stuck. Would you like assistance? Would you like a short adjournment? A short adjournment will be called.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I suppose we'll have to start all over again, because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. I'm told we don't have to introduce the case. Then we were at the stage where we just had appearances. Once again, Mr. Delic, as I said the other day, I know you do know that you took the declaration to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth, but it's still my responsibility to remind you that you are still bound by that declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Thank you very much. Judge Harhoff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Questioned by the Court: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Good morning, General.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have a single question relating to one part -- one part of your testimony. I think it was Thursday last, on the 20th of September. And the issue goes to your knowledge of how the 3rd Corps was organised. Let me read out to you what you said on Thursday. The Prosecution asked you - and for reference, this is page 2750, if you are interested to know, line number 7 - the -- the Prosecution asked you: "Do you know which units of the 35th Division were involved in Operation Farz?" And your answer was: "No, I can only guess. What I saw in Vozuca was that there were probably the 7th Muslim Division, the El Mujahid Detachment. I saw men with beards." These were your words, and we also heard you give an answer to the Prosecution's question where the Prosecution asked you: "General Delic, other than the ARBiH 2nd Corps units, what military force or forces were deployed along the Ozren front?" And your answer was, as follows: "From what I know, those were units of the 3rd Corps of the BH army, which were then grouped in the 35th Division of the 3rd Corps." Obviously the issue of how the 3rd Corps was organised is a sensitive issue in this case, so I don't know if I could do something perhaps rather unusual by asking the parties if any of the parties would have -- would be so kind as to explore with the witness his knowledge of how the 3rd Corps was organised; and, of course, in particular, if he knows whether the El Mujahid Detachment was under the command of the 3rd Corps. And if he knows, then just how that was organised. This is my question that I have to the witness. And rather than putting the question myself, I'd rather I leave it to the parties to seek to explore this issue a bit with the witness, if that is acceptable. Mr. Prosecutor, Madam Vidovic, if you have anything to ...?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm not sure if -- if this current witness can take that much further, but we certainly will have additional witnesses, including the witness who's scheduled to appear later today, who might be in a better position to address these issues. So the Prosecution view would be that, I think we've taken this as far as we could with this witness. Perhaps if the Bench wants to ask him additional questions concerning the basis of the knowledge concerning the evidence he's already given, certainly that would be an appropriate position, but -- but our view would be we have witnesses who are better placed to address that issue, including one who is scheduled to appear later this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, we share the same view as the Prosecution and would support that. It's the Defence's position that this witness was not in a position to know well the structure of the 3rd Corps, and so we would prefer it if this matter was dealt with in -- with subsequent witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Very well. I accept this. So I have no further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I've got only three issues --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, apologies. The issue involved Vozuca itself, not the operation in Vozuca. That's why there was this confusion. I knew - and it is undoubtedly so - that on the other side the largest involved unit was the 3rd Corps, or rather, its 35th Division. The question you put concerned the units which arrived in Vozuca on -- about which we saw the video clip. That was the only difference. It -- the fact of the matter was not Farz or Uragan; rather, the units that were present in Vozuca. And this is what you wanted to know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: It was indeed. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I have just three issues to raise with you, sir. The first one relates to maybe the need to check whether the transcript is correct. At page 2776, line 2, this is what was said about -- this is what -- I just want to get the ... Yeah, at line 2, you were asked the question: "While we were celebrating, somebody is standing guard up there, isn't it? We are fighting now too. We are as close here -- as here. He tells me, "President." And then Awad Aiman: "We imprisoned one Chetnik who says that he served the military in Doboj." And then you say, "We have some six teachers imprisoned." This is what's written here. I didn't hear "six teachers." I heard something else. Let me read to you the entire answer that you gave to remind you so that you may be -- maybe you may be able to remember. It says: "Mr. Delic: We have some six teachers imprisoned. There are those who have stayed alive, but I don't know if they -- they still are. There were -- generally, there were many of them who --" and then something cannot be understood "-- for a month. They created biggest problems for us. We launched four attacks from 6.00 a.m. to 1.00 a.m. We couldn't break through in this central area. We broke out at 7.00 here on the axis between Lozna and Seona. We broke through there and we were almost close to Djurica Vis in order to get connected. However with God's help, things developed for the better. Even in the time of peace at training, I wouldn't expect better." This is during the clip. This is what you are supposed to have said during the clip. Now, to the best of your recollection, did you say you have six teachers or did you say something else?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, last time I spoke to Her Honour about this. I believe that the translation was good. The information I received was that there were five to six professors or teachers - I don't know what they were - who were captured. I also explained to Her Honour that one does not only take prisoner of those who are alive and well in wartime but also those who are slightly or seriously wounded. I didn't know what the situation was at the time. I have to tell you that I did not have in my possession full information. There may have been these five to six, but there were the total of 80 captured; whereas, for the three days of the action, there were 163 prisoners in all. I believe that the translation was good and that this is indeed how the conversation unfolded. I don't know exactly what the President asked, and so this is my answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I just want to be sure that you were talking about six teachers. Thank you very much. Then on Thursday last week we were still talking when the Judge here asked you about something else. And I would like to -- to follow up what we were talking about at that time. And if we could please have Exhibit 410 on the screen. Now, this exhibit is made up of five photographs. I would like us to go through each one of those photographs. I would like you to show us those people that you said were either soldiers or officers of the El Mujahid Detachment. Do you see anyone on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. But if you'll allow me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, if I'll allow you?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I may not have been quite clear in my previous answer. These were not civilian teachers. These were soldiers who were teachers by profession. So as to avoid any confusion, those captured were members of the Army of Republika Srpska, who were otherwise teachers by profession.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much for that clarification. Let's now deal with this -- there are going to be five photographs shown here. On this photograph here, do you see anybody here that you said was a soldier or an officer of the El Mujahid Detachment?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we see the next photograph, please, of the same exhibit. Can we enlarge it, please. Do you see anybody here?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, you said that I should not speculate. I will assume that these two -- oh, we've lost the image. In the background, behind President Izetbegovic and the commander of the 35th Division and Mr. Sakib Mahmuljin, the general, there are three persons out of whom two have beards; one of them wearing a white cap. And I believe the two of them were members.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think they were members otherwise of the 7th Muslim.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm not asking you about the 7th Muslim, sir. I'm asking you about the El Mujahid Detachment. I see red dots on two persons. Are those the persons that you're identifying?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can you go to the next photo, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, please. Could -- well, I, yeah, let's save that and give it an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, that will be Exhibit number 424.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can we go to the next photograph, please. Do you see anybody here that you would recognise as being an El Mujahid Detachment soldier or officer?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I've been thinking about this for quite a while, but I have to react. My apologies to Their Honours; however, I am quite concerned with this line of questioning. At no point in time did the witness say that he was familiar with the structure of the El Mujahid Detachment or their officers. The fact that he sees a person who is bearded cannot bear any weight. And I'm really concerned about such questions. I believe the witness was quite direct in his answer to Her Honour Judge Lattanzi's question. And I'm quite concerned with the fact that the witness is called upon to further speculate and to point at matters he is not certain about. I wish to state this for the transcript -- for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, this -- the basis for my questions is the testimony of the witness. The witness testified, and I quoted the testimony to the witness. He said he saw soldiers or officers of the El Mujahid Detachment at this celebration. Now I'm just asking him to tell us who are those people that he saw that he identified as officers or soldiers of the El Mujahid. And you will remember -- you're saying he answered Judge Lattanzi's questions. Judge Lattanzi asked those questions while I was in the middle of asking these questions last Thursday. And I left it at that point because I knew I would still have this opportunity to ask these questions. I'm not asking the witness to speculate. I'm asking him to tell us who are these people that he -- he said in his testimony he saw who are soldiers or officers of the El Mujahid. If he says he doesn't see them here, it's up to him to say he doesn't see them. Mr. Delic, did you answer to this one?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What did you -- what was your answer? Just to remind me.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I did not see a single person who could possibly be from the El Mujahid Detachment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Fine. That was the third photograph. Can we go to the fourth one.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can say the same thing I said about the previous image.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What --

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that this person on the right-hand side is a member of the detachment. Although, I repeat, I can't say what his capacity there was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We -- I'm not asking for capacities. I'm not asking you for structure. Thank you very much. Is that the only one?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I can see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can we see the next picture, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Oh, thank you very much. Can this picture with that mark be admitted into evidence and be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 425.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can we go to the last picture, please.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. You've -- you've made a cross on two faces here. Can this picture also be admitted into evidence and be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, Exhibit number -- [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number 426 [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I guess that's the end of the pictures. Just before we leave this point, Madam Vidovic, you raised amongst the points that you raised when you objected that this witness says he knows nothing about the structure. You'll realise I've asked him nothing about the structure of that corps. The last issue I want to raise with you, sir, is this: Can you -- you can confirm for me that you are retired from the army in 2000?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. On the 1st of October, 2000.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: All right. And the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina ended in -- in 1995; am I right?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. With the signing of the Dayton Accords and the order on the cease-fire. The order was issued on the 11th of October, 1992, requiring us to cease all hostilities and to engage in the negotiations at Camp David.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About the -- and then in Dayton and later on in Paris too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. All I need is the -- the date. After the war, did the army still use packet communication systems?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, the system remained in use -- in use for quite a while, and I believe it is still in use today. Of course, for urgent matters, for communications that have to be urgently transmitted and such like.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And there were other forms of communication for -- that did not involve the packet communication system?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Among others, couriers, the normal wire connections - that is to say, telephone and telefax connections - depending on the confidentiality of the document involved, and the needs of the army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I have no further questions for you. Any questions arising? Mr. Mundis?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No questions from the Prosecution. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Robson?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Just a few questions, Your Honour. Further cross-examination by Mr. Robson:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General Delic, on Friday you were asked by Judge Lattanzi the following: "If illegal activities were committed by soldiers or officers at the lower level, was the commander of the unit duty-bound to sanction those illegal activities?" And to that question, you agreed that they were. Can you remember giving that response?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I am of the same view today. I believe Her Honour was quite right. The first person involved was supposed to react immediately and was -- and others were supposed to follow suit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You then said that the low-ranking commander should inform his immediate superior, who should in turn propose certain measures. And in this regard, I'd like to show you a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, if the witness could please be shown P1493.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, could you just confirm for us that what we see on the screen is a document entitled "Order on enforcement of the rules of the international military law in the armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina"?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's precisely so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we could scroll down to the bottom of the page in the English version and go on to page 2 in the B/C/S version, please. General, could you confirm for us that this order was issued by the President of the Presidency, Alija Izetbegovic, on the 23rd of August, 1992?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This order was issued by him, by the President, and by the commander of the armed forces, the late Alija Izetbegovic, on behalf of the Presidency, on the 23rd of August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we could return back to the first page in the B/C/S version. Are you familiar with this order, General?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. We drafted something similar already in May of 1992 which concerned the application of international laws of war in wartime. I didn't receive the document itself, but I received instructions from my superior. I suppose that as corps commander he must have received the order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if we look at Article 1 of the order, General, it's right that this article provides that: "The armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina shall enforce the rules of the international military law in the armed conflict"?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And we can see that in Article 1 it also defines what is meant by "international military law"; is that so?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if we look at Article 2, is it right that this provides that "The commanders of the units and each member of the armed forces individually is responsible for the enforcement of the rules of the international military law"?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This means that all members of the armed forces have that duty, not just the commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if we go into the next part of Article 2, it provides that: "The competent commander is obliged to start procedure to pronounce legal sanctions against persons who violate the rules of the international military law." Is that so?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was commented upon by Her Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, would you agree with me that under Article 2, commanders of the units at all levels were obliged to take steps to enforce international military law?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that would mean, for example, that if the commander at the very lowest level discovered that one of his subordinates had committed a criminal offence, he would be obliged to take steps to start a procedure against that subordinate.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, within his competence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Okay. Your Honours, please could this document be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] The document is admitted into evidence -- may it please -- I beg your pardon. The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 427.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Robson, this is an interesting point that you have raised in extension of Judge Lattanzi's original question about this. My understanding of the situation in the ABiH was that due to the fact that the original JNA was being split at the time, what the ABiH had left was in many cases soldiers who had received very little training. And so I would like you to explore with the witness if any training then or any information was then offered to the combatants as to what was implied in the international customary military law and the treaties signed by Bosnia. I mean, you get my point. One thing is that you have on paper is that everybody was supposed to know about this. But did -- did they in fact?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, you've heard the Judge's question. We can see that this order provides obligations on the part of the armed forces. From your knowledge of what occurred during the 2nd Corps, were any concrete steps taken to introduce measures so that subordinate units and soldiers became familiar with these international law obligations?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. On the 29th of May, 1992, from the corps command, I personally wrote a brief instruction to the troops and commanding officers in relation to the application of international laws of war and the definition of "war booty," because there were such persons who thought that a chicken were war booty, among other things. We did it right at the outset. You have to bear in mind that in this army, which was initially the Territorial Defence, there were no military officers who had been schooled and taught about these matters. If we look at the percentages, then there were less than 5 per cent trained officers. You only had the commander and his closest associates in a headquarters who were professional soldiers. For this reason, it was quite difficult. But I can tell you that as concerned the 2nd Corps, the situation improved in time. We also managed, with the assistance of international organizations that were present in the area, to train soldiers and members of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, as far as we were able to, to fully adhere to the provisions of international laws of war. I can also tell you that in the area of Tuzla municipality, as early as the 16th or the 17th of May, thanks to several lawyers who were attached to the General Staff, we managed to discuss these matters. One of them was Judge Vildana Heljic, who was one of the persons who launched this initiative. And this bore fruit in the first material -- written material that was distributed, circulated among soldiers on the 29th of May, 1992. I can tell you the situation thus far as it concerned my own unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And before we leave this issue, General, we discussed it in Article 2 of this order that the commanders of the units were responsible for the enforcement of international military law. Can you tell us what is meant by "the commanders of units"?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under "commanders of units," it is meant all levels of commanding and commanders, starting with the commander of the battalion. From battalion level to brigade level or autonomous or independent detachments and brigades and divisions, municipal staffs, district staff at that time, then corps, up to the highest level, on behalf of the joint command, the commander of the army of the BiH, and the commander of the General Staff. So up to the top.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's right to say, isn't it, General, that obligations relating to international military law were also set out in other regulations and legislation as well?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether this was part of all rules and laws. Of course, those -- that's what over the war produced and distributed, this provision must have been in them. For the earlier, in the former SFRJ, it was used as far as it concerned technical matters, the rules of military equipment, weapons, some rules about units and some others. Although, as far as I know, those also contained the provision on the necessity to abide by international laws of war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, General. Now, Judge Lattanzi also asked you some questions about the 7th Muslim Brigade. You would agree with me at no stage was the 7th Muslim Brigade a subordinate unit of the 2nd Corps during the war.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's right, isn't it, that during the war you -- at no time did you receive any information about the structure of the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. It's only that commander of the 7th Muslim, General Brzina, helped me to establish the 9th Muslim, because I did not know what the Shura was, which was diametrically opposed to the system of control and command that I knew. So he came over to help me establish this unit, and this was in August 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's right is that the battalions of the 7th Muslim Brigade were located a considerable distance away from where you were based in Tuzla. They were in Zenica, Travnik, and Kakanj. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where they were, but I presume that most of them were in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you don't know where the battalions of the 7th Muslim Brigade were located. Can it -- would you agree with me that --

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, my answer is "no."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that your level of knowledge about that brigade was such that you cannot exclude the possibility that there were members -- that Bosnian Croats or Bosnian Serbs were members of that brigade?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Honourable Judge warned me against guessing. I said -- I guessed 80, 90 per cent, but my true answer is "no." But taking into consideration how I established this 9th Muslim Brigade, there wasn't supposed to be an atheist as a member of the 9th Brigade who was not a Bosniak. I know that there were no other people other than Bosniaks in that brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not asking about the 9th Muslim Brigade. We're -- we're focusing on the 7th Muslim Brigade. As I understand your answer, you have just confirmed you cannot --

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- exclude the possibility that the Bosnian Croats or Bosnian Serbs were members.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in the final point, General, Judge Moloto today put to you that the men that we looked at in the photographs were soldiers or officers of the El Mujahid Detachment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let's just -- let's just correct that. I didn't put it to him. I asked him. I didn't put anything to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Okay. Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I just asked him to identify.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: I'll rephrase that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, this morning we discussed -- you discussed with the Trial Chamber photographs that were shown to you last week by the Prosecutor. Please, can you help me with something, because I'm now rather confused about your evidence. As I understood your response last week, you told the Trial Chamber that you could not be sure that those men were members of the El Mujahid Detachment. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I maintain that today. I presume, but I wasn't sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you don't know whether those men that you spoke about today were members of the El Mujahid Detachment or whether they were members of an international humanitarian organisation or whether they were there in some completely different capacity. Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, I arrived a bit late at that function. I presumed -- and I saw them as they were, and I presumed that they may be them. You are right. If I were not guessing, I would say "no," but this is a matter of my feeling whether they were or they were not Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, General. This brings us to the conclusion of your testimony. Thank you very much for taking time off to come and testify. You are now excused. You may stand down. Travel well home. I'm sorry we could not finish with you last week to enable you to spend the weekend at home, but that's how these things happen. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I guess this would be a convenient time to take the break. We'll take the break and come back at quarter to. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. May you please make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may be seated. Please do sit down and make yourself comfortable. Yes, Mr. Mundis. Or Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Neuner:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, witness. What is your name?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Fadil Hasanagic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When were you born?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: The 25th of May, 1948.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I seek permission to lead the witness through his military career.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Beginning in 1969, you went for two years to the military academy in Belgrade and attended courses in the field of engineering; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in 1971 you continued your education in the same field in Karlovac.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in 1972, you entered the JNA.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And until 1980, you stayed at the training centre in Karlovac.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And until 1985, you were chief of the engineers in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From 1985 until 1991, you were commander of an engineering battalion in Cakovec.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in 1984 and 1986, you again attended courses at the military academy in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in 1991, you became the chief of engineers in Varos.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In November 1991, you went to the 2nd military district of the JNA in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In April 1992, you left the JNA and joined the Regional Staff in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In September 1992, you became the commander of this regional staff.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Of the Regional Staff of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In December 1992, you became the commander of the 511th Brigade in Bihac.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In June 1993, you became the chief of staff of the 5th Corps in Bihac.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in February 1994, you became commander of the OG Bosna.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In March 1995, you became commander of the 35th Division, a position you held until the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after the war, you held four positions; namely, the chief of engineers in the army.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, chief of the engineers of the army. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The assistant commander for training.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, assistant to the chief of staff for training.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And chief of staff of the 5th Corps, as well as deputy commander of the 5th Corps.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was from this last position that you retired in April 2000, holding the rank of brigadier.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Brigade general, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigade general. Thank you for this clarification. I want to focus on your time when you were commander of the OG Bosna, starting in February 1994. Where was the headquarters of OG Bosna?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: At Zavidovici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you just confirmed that in March 1995 you became the commander of the 35th Division. What was the relationship between OG Bosna and this 35th Division?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: There was no major distinction. OG was a temporary composition and later on the 35th Division was established as a permanent unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So where was the headquarters of this 35th Division?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: At the same place, in Zavidovici, the same place where previously it was the headquarters of the OG.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And which brigades were in this 35th Division?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: 328 from Zavidovici with five battalions; 327th Brigade, mobilised from Maglaj, also five battalions; and 329th Mountain Brigade, from Kakanj, with three battalions. Later on we established three manoeuvre battalions: The 3rd, the 4th, and the 5th Manoeuvre Battalion. And, of course, staff units at the level of company and platoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to whom was this 35th Division subordinated to?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: The 35th Division was subordinated to the command of the 3rd Corps of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We talked a moment ago about the OG Bosna. To which unit was this OG Bosna subordinated to?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: To the 3rd Corps of the army as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher, I want to have some maps distributed. I have copies for all the Judges as well as for the Defence and the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I want you to do, Witness, is to -- to lay out the eastern front line on this map of OG Bosna and at the time when you came to Zavidovici in 1994 to take up your duty as OG Bosna commander.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: It cannot be seen. There are several other features.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness -- interpreters note: Could the witness speak into a microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This was the demarcation line with the 2nd Corps of the army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you mark a "1" next to this demarcation line.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you mark now the eastern front line of OG Bosna at the time you arrived to OG Bosna.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry to do this to you, Mr. Neuner. I had been looking at the map, the hard copy you gave. Can the witness please show us the first question -- the first line that you asked him to show, the east -- the eastern front line of the OG Bosna. Where was it? I can't see it now because the lines look alike here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I think the witness is about or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You said he must write a "1" next to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yeah, the "1" next to it was -- on the button there where the border to the 2nd Corps was, I understood the witness to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if the Prosecutor could clarify with the witness which was the zone of responsibility so that we know what we are talking about when we refer to "western" and "eastern" side so that we can find our bearings on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I will.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, the line you were just drawing, in relation to that line, where was the AOR of the OG Bosna?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: To the west of this line. To the west was Mahnjaca, and then on the right-hand side this line, Podsjelovo, Krcevine, Malovan, Popov Osoje, Radonivlje [phoen]. And then Osturic [phoen], Visic, Zedni Vrh, Vranovine, and then a connection and link up with the 2nd Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you just continue the line which is crossing the River Krivaja now to connect with, ultimately, number 1 in the lower right-hand side. How was the AOR -- or what was the frontier of the AOR of the OG Bosna when you came? If you could just indicate that.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And if you could mark a "2" at the upper part of that line, indicating that this is the line.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you now mark where Vozuca is.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Encircle it and mark it with a 3, please.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question to you is: At that time when you came in 1994, who -- which army had held Vozuca, had control over Vozuca?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: 1st and 2nd and 3rd Brigade and several brigades came from some other parts, from Prijedor, Srbacka Brigade and other brigades and the special units of theirs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And with "theirs," which army are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: The enemy army, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And which is the enemy army? Could you state the abbreviation of it -- for it.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: The Army of the Republika Srpska, VRS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you left Zavidovici at the end of the war, which army had control over Vozuca?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: When I left Zavidovici, Vozuca had been liberated. Our army had control over Vozuca; that is to say, the army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when moved the ABiH into Vozuca?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: In September of 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What military significance had Vozuca while it was not taken by the ABiH -- not yet taken by the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: The Zavidovici-Ribnica road ran along it, connecting the Tuzla and Zenica cantons and Zavidovici and Banovici. The 40 or so kilometres of that road enabled one to cross the territory. Otherwise, one had to take a detour of some 200 or 300 kilometres to reach Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I was waiting for the witness to finish. Can I ask my learned friend to first lay a foundation for his question. Like, for instance, in this case, whether it had any significance or importance, because the question as it was put now stated what significance it had.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I've put the question as it was. I will try in my future questioning to take my colleague's -- my learned friend's suggestions into consideration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you mark with a "4" where that road is you just talked about.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next to the "X" you just made, can you mark a "4".

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: For -- for those of us who don't understand, Mr. Neuner, I would imagine that that road is a line? So if you could show which way that road goes and where it leads. Maybe put another -- a "5" at the end of the 40-kilometre stretch.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please mark, if it's on the map, where the road was leading to with a "5", the road which was at the time under VRS control, I understood.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: I am tracing it with my pencil. This is where Ribnica is and...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness repeat the rest of his answer. It was -- we couldn't hear it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you repeat the answer. After "Ribnica," what was at Ribnica?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Ribnica was free territory in the direction of Banovici and Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By "free territory," you mean which army held it?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: The BH army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you could clarify, which part, west or east, of number 5 was held by the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Since this was not within my area of responsibility, I can't say. I only know that the territory to the east of Ribnica was under the control of the BH army. That's where the 2nd Corps was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. We heard from you that once you left the 35th Division that area formally held by the VRS was in ABiH hands. Could you explain what efforts, if any, in 1994 were taken to gain control over the VRS-held area.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: The area of responsibility of the OG Bosna, later to be the area of responsibility of the 35th Division, was quite a difficult one to control because of the lie of the terrain and because of the buildup of the forces there, especially Blizna, Podsjelovo, Krcevine, Malovan, and then to the south-east of the Krivaja River, Zedni Vhr, Vranovinje, Mahovski Vrh and other. The enemy was constantly active out of that area. Not only from the villages I mentioned, but also the towns of Zavidovici and Maglaj were under fire from that area, these towns, that is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what efforts by the ABiH to gain control in 1994 were done?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: At the time we didn't have enough troops or weapons. We got engaged in actions to move the front lines for -- such as the ones against Paljenik on several occasions in 1994 where there were attempts at liberating that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I show you a document. And PT number is 1845. This is a document which will appear on your screen from the 24th of October, 1994. It's entitled "Decision of attack" by Mr. Mahmuljin and sent to the Operational Group Bosna. And I'm interested in the upper right-hand side of the document where it says "Manevar 94." Can you explain to the Judges what "Manevar 94" means.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Every action, battle, or operation that was launched had a title, a name of its own. This name was just as any other name of an operation such as Proljece is spring. That's all there is to it; there's nothing special about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the objective of Manevar 94?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: The objective of Manevar 1994 was to take control of Greda Podsjelovo -- or, rather, Podsjelovo ridge, Maljine and Paljenik ridge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: It's Malovan ridge. Can the witness please be asked to speak more slowly when he's mentioning place names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you mention place names, please speak a little bit slower for the translator. Can you on the map next to you encircle Greda Podsjelovo, please.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And mark a "6" next to it, please.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I wish to tender this document we just discussed with the witness into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 428.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Exhibit 428. That is the map?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Not the map --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Oh, the document. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yeah, the document itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to show you the next exhibit, dating one day earlier before the document we just saw. PT is 1843. Again, an order by Mahmuljin sent to OG Bosna. And I'm interested in number 1 of that document. Mentioning is made here of teams from the 3rd Corps command who were sent to the -- to you, the commander of the Bosna OG. Were these teams indeed coming?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were within my area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was discussed on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: The preparation for the action we just looked at, based on the commander's decision, was discussed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Preparation of Manevar, yes?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this action was launched or was not launched finally?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Nevertheless, can I tender this document into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 429.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to take you to 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I -- can I just, before you take the witness to 1995 -- I may just have missed something here. PT1845 has been admitted into evidence as Exhibit 428. Prior to that, PT1493 was admitted as Exhibit 427. In between those two exhibits, I think a map was shown to the witness and the witness has been making markings on this map. I'm not quite sure what the fate of that map is.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We are going on with further operations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And at the end of these operations, I will tender the document -- the map into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm aware of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I just wanted to -- okay. I'm pleased you are. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I wanted to move to 1995. And you informed us, finally in September Vozuca -- or the ABiH established control over Vozuca. What I want to know from you: How many combat operations were necessary that finally in September 1995 the ABiH moved into Vozuca.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: The Vozuca operation took place in September of 1995. Prior to that, several actions were needed in order to take up tactical -- operational tactical positions and to come closer to Vozuca. In short, it involved three actions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you start with the first action. What was the name of the first action?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: The first one took place in April, south-east of the Krivaja River, and it was called Sabur.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you mark on the map next to you where the gravity of this combat operation Sabur was with a "7", please.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: [Marks] Number 5 or number 7?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Moving on to the next operation, which operation was following Sabur?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: After Sabur action, in May of 1995 the Proljece operation took place with the objective of taking up Podsjelovo ridge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you mark with an 8 -- or encircle and mark with an "8" where the main line of attack of Proljece was?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Which operation followed then?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: In the month of July, there followed the Proljece II action with the objective of taking up the features of Krcevine, Malovan and Malije Gaj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you maybe indicate with an arrow in which direction the attack towards Krcevine and Malovan, which direction this combat operation was taking. And mark a "9" next to these arrows.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you encircle Krcevine, please, and mark a "10" next to it.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Which was the next combat operation?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: The next combat operation took place in September of 1995, which was one of the operations in the area with the participation of two corps of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us the 35th Division was part of the 3rd Corps. Could you indicate the main axis of attack of the 3rd Corps 35th Division in this September operation.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: The corps commander did not give the main axis of the attack. It gave axis 1, which was the one running in the direction of the Paljenik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just draw an arrow and encircle "Paljenik." Please mark an "11" next to it.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said "the main axis of attack." Was there another axis?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: The other forces of the corps probably had other axes to pursue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Now, Your Honours, I wish to tender this document -- this map into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The map is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 430.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You just introduced us to Operation Sabur in April 1994. I wish to show you PT number 2000. This is an order, again, from Mahmuljin from the 31st of March, 1995. It is sent to the 35th Division commander - meaning you - and it's entitled -- it just says "Order." And then it says: "Preparations for active combat operations." If you look at number 1, what is Mr. Mahmuljin doing here?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it is quite right for the Prosecutor to state the date of the document, who produced the document, to whom it was sent before we see the document, but even before we were able to see the document, the Prosecutor already states that this is the order by Mahmuljin. Perhaps the witness should first be allowed to look at the document, to establish who wrote the document, and to whom, and only then should the question follow of what Mahmuljin's intentions were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I propose the following course of action: I'm doing this to save a certain amount of time, because it takes some ten seconds until the image appears. I can -- to take on board the suggestion from my learned colleague, I can introduce the document the way I did. And once it is on the screen, I can ask the witness to confirm what I said and then move on to the question. If this is an agreeable course of action.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That -- yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this would be quite fine in principle; however, it is not right in this case because we haven't seen who signed the document. We can't say that this is Mahmuljin's order if it is stated in the signature block that it was signed on his behalf. I believe we have to establish this fact first. We can't see the signature block in the English version. Perhaps this is something the Prosecutor should first explore with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I fully understand the suggestion of my learned colleague. And fully understand --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Actually, when laying the basis for admission, I think the witness must give answers, not you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise the signature here?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Somebody signed for the commander, on his behalf. I don't recognise the signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I need to correct myself. I before stated that it was Mr. Mahmuljin. Somebody signed for the 3rd Corps commander. And I will endeavour to not make such comments in the future.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning back to my question, I wanted to ask with regard to number 1, what are you ordered -- or what is ordered here by somebody signing for the 3rd Corps commander?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: The person who signed on behalf of the corps commander, I don't know whether he has that competence, to re-subordinate a unit to the command of the 35th Division. So this is the order re-subordinating units for the purposes of the impending combat actions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was this order carried out?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Yes. There were other orders too, and on the basis of these orders the re-subordination to the 35th Division was indeed carried out for the purposes of these combat actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I wish to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Just before you tender it, I think I -- I heard you say in one of your introductory comments about this document that it was addressed to the witness. I'm trying to look to see where it shows that it was addressed to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If you look at the second page of the English translation, you see in the first hyphen -- this is the "sent to" column.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. And did the witness see this?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: In his version, it is on the first page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: -- which is displayed the whole time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you so much. The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 431.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The next exhibit to be shown is exhibit 2014, PT2014. It is an order to attack. And I'm asking the witness to confirm this once it is displayed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see "Order to attack" here on the document?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: "Order to attack."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May I suggest this, Mr. Neuner: Just so that you don't get objections, get the witness to tell you whether he recognises this document, if -- and tell you what it is, who it comes from, who it's addressed to, and what it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let him testify.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you look at the upper right-hand corner, it says "Sabur 95" there.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: That's the name of the action concerned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the English version, it says "illegible" there, but if we enlarge exactly the B/C/S, it -- as was just done, we see -- can you read this out, what you can read there?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: "Defence of the republic. Military secret. Strictly confidential, Sabur 95. To be submitted by courier."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we look at the last page in the B/C/S only, whose signature is this?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you tell me, you were signing this order for attack?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you -- were you authorised to do this?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's my order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who authorised you?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: The corps commander had previously approved this action, and it was on that basis that I wrote the order. The order was signed by the corps commander, as was the appendix to my order, which was a map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We will come to this in a moment. Who is the corps commander? From which corps?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: The commander of the 3rd Corps, Sakib Mahmuljin.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I wish to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 432.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I wish to show you another document, PT2009. And in the English translation, it says: "List of documents."

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is a list of documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To which activity is this relating to?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: It is related to the Sabur action.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there under number 4 unit is mentioned. Why are signatures provided there?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Every unit had to receive the order, an excerpt of the map, and other documents necessary for the implementation of the action.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can I please tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 433.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We were already talking about the month of April when Sabur was taking place. I want to show you document PT2016 and explain to the Judges what this is about. First of all -- it just disappeared. Could you say whose signature this is, if we scroll down in the B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: It's my signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you look at number 5 of the document from 7 of April, 1995, I believe in the English it is the second page.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: I don't have the image.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could --

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Now it's appeared.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the English version, it's number -- paragraph -- page 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Page 2, paragraph ...?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: "Prepare the deployment area for the detachment in the base area of the Dvanaesti, the Twelfth Kilometre."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where is the Twelfth Kilometre?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: The Twelfth Kilometre is a feature, an area. 12 kilometres away from Zavidovici. It's a fork in the road with some edifices and fortifications. Several roads intersect there. There was water there as well. And previously, units from Kakanj had been deployed there within my composition, and this is why I instructed the corps commander that they be deployed at the Twelfth Kilometre facility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say there was water there. What water was there?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Drinking water, of course. One of the elements that is necessary for a base camp is to have running water, electricity, roads, and if there's no grid electricity, then a generator, that there is -- there are facilities for training, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say in page 41, line 12 that they should be deployed at the Twelfth Kilometre. Whom are you referring to by "they"?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: The El Mujahedin Detachment. This is what I meant to be deployed at the Twelfth Kilometre.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I wish to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 434.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You talked earlier about Operation Proljece, that it occurred in May 1995. And in relation to this, I want to show you document number 2101.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's document 2001, right? Not 201.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: PT?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you look at the upper right-hand corner of the document, you find here "Proljece - 95." Do you see this?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise the document?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who signed the document? If we can go to the last page, please. In the B/C/S only.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's my signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you authorised to sign this operation or this -- this order?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: The order, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who approved that you signed such an order?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: The corps commander approved. I sign an order, sent it to the corps commander for his approval.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And which corps commander are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: The commander of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when did you get his approval? Before or after signing? This document?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: The process to produce this document is a lengthy one. There are many steps and actions to be performed at division command and at levels of commands of subordinated units, brigades, et cetera. And when this process is finished, I propose to the corps commander on the basis of our estimate that we should do this or that. The corps commander may or may not agree. If he agreed, then I draft a document such as this one, this order. I send it to the corps commander for approval. Of course, this is accompanied by a map. And only when the commander has approved can I embark on carrying out that idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I wish to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 435.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I wish to show you document 2075. The previous document was from the 24th of May. This document is from the 15th of May. Nine days earlier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could please confirm the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Sorry, I see 19th of May. I think I have here the wrong document.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: It says here "19th of May."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yeah. Sorry, the English translation misguided me. It says "15th of May."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And what is the correct date? 19th of May?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I see that the translation and the B/C/S don't match. I believe I withdraw that document and come back to it at a later stage. I see the B/C/S is from the 19th --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: They're two different documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yeah, it has also different BROJ numbers. I withdraw the document at this point in time. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner, while we're looking for the next document, could you please just clarify one thing: I wasn't sure about the -- the nature of the last document we saw, Exhibit 435.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: What we had on the screen, was that the -- the final order after the corps commander had approved it or was it still before?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I will ask.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Hasanagic, you heard the remark by the Judge. The document we saw a moment ago was from the 24th of May, 1995. And you signed it. At the time you signed it, did you have the approval of Mr. Mahmuljin or did this follow the approval?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: The order is drafted beforehand and is sent to the command -- corps commander's approval. And then the order is the final document that is sent to the 3rd Corps command for approval.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But when you signed this document, as we just saw, at this point in time of your signature, did you have the approval in your pocket or were you waiting for it?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: I waited for the -- the approval, and the document is approved when the commander writes and signs in the top left corner "I approve," and then signs his name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: All right. Now, I can't remember, did the corps commander's signature follow?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We have it here in front on the screen still. I don't see the commander's signature, but maybe you have been the author of the document and you remember. Did you at a later point in time get the 3rd Corps commander's written approval for this action?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did receive approval for this action. I could not proceed without that approval, because some of the corps units participated in that action.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I want to go to PT2105. And we just need the B/C/S. Could you explain to the Judges once it is displayed what this is.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: This constitutes a decision to attack. Spring 1995, operation 1995 action. This is an integral part of the order. It is an appendix to the order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if we just look at the right side where the yellow and orange markings are made, we have the letters "EL-M" next to it. Could you indicate what abbreviation you're using here. "EL-M," what does this stand for?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: That's the El Mujahid Detachment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And below there, it says: "4 mnb." What is this standing for?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: This is the 4th Manoeuvre Battalion. And then at the rear, you say -- you see "the 2nd Manoeuvre Battalion."

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I wish to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 436.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to move to PT2138 now. If you could just explain. It's displayed on your screen. What are you doing here?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are we going to see the English version?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So is this your signature? Is my first question.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what are you doing here?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: After we captured the Podsjelovo ridge which the El Mujahid Detachment and the other units shown on the map were there, and given that Zavidovici had been and 15, 16 other villages had been fired upon from that ridge of Podsjelovo and given that the operation was successful, I issued to all the units this certificate of merit because there was no other way that I could commend them for the success, because the town of Zavidovici and the surrounding villages were no longer fired at from that feature. And this document, this certificate of merit, is a document whereby I thanked them for what they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I wish --

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Of course, there was a rule book which regulated this matter. And I did not write those rules. I received them from my superior command.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I wish to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 437.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
