utterances.text: I want to move to a completely different topic, military training. I want to ask you: What is the purpose of military training?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: The purpose of military training is to train troops and officers to accomplish the tasks that they were given.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was training or military training conducted in the AOR of the 35th Division in 1995?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is one of the elements of combat readiness. Maybe the first one, if I remember correctly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where was such training conducted?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Training was performed by battalion commanders in their areas of deployment, commanders of brigades in their areas of deployment, or by grouping units for certain combat actions at a single place, and this is the way that we did it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you name the main places of training in your AOR?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: I said it was carried out at battalion and brigade level. At the division level, we organised training on the Ninth Kilometre, in the area of the village of Cardak because there was a school building with enough classrooms. There was a gym as well. Logistical support could be provided. There were five, six other buildings that were not destroyed. There were playing fields. There was an area where you could train personnel. So under our estimates, that facility was appropriate to group certain forces there before certain either attack or defence actions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mm-hm. And when did the training at the Ninth Kilometre start?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: I think that training at the Ninth Kilometre started for the Spring II action, and we used that model for training for the Operation September 95.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And which unit participated in the training or military training for Spring or Proljece 95 II or Proljece II action?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: It was organised by brigades. Given that this was a smaller scale action, each brigade or those units that were earmarked for attack would train with them. And this was why we grouped such units. The other part of general training was conducted at the areas of deployment of brigades.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I just ask: Is Spring II action the same thing as Proljece 95 II action?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's Proljece II or Spring II. That is -- that was in July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you just clarify for Your Honour, when was the action Proljece? In which month of 1995?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Action Spring was in May. Proljece II was in July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the training, I understood you, was for Proljece II?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, for July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I show you document 2457. You see the B/C/S. Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [French on English channel]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now I'm hearing French. I'm hearing French translation.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can you hear me, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The French booth was on the wrong channel. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Only now when you say it again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document, was my question?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: It says on this document: "Regular combat report." I am about to see whether I signed it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we move to the last page of the B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: I think that this is not my signature, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's enlarged now. Okay. Maybe I can ask you about the content and you may remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we also see the end of the English. [Microphone not activated] Okay. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I want to ask you to have a look at section 2, entitled "Training plan." In B/C/S, it's page 1. In English, page 3 of this document. Okay. Maybe if I -- I think in B/C/S it's -- no. No, it's under -- this is 2473? Is this document 2473, if I may ask?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: I can't see --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, if I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic. Just a second, Mr. Neuner. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, as far as I understand, this is document 2457, so we are at cross-purposes. What we see on the screen is PT2457.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We are at 2457. I apologise. I have confused. I want to look at -- have the witness look at the second page of the B/C/S in the third hyphen, starting with [B/C/S spoken] "komandir." And in English, it is page 3, the second-last hyphen from the bottom, starting with "the team of the 35th Division command."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you find this portion? Mr. Hasanagic?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: I can see it now, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain what the team of the 35th Division command is doing here.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: The team from the 35th Division of command visited the Cardak training centre, as per its purview, and inspected -- and inspected the training under the leadership of El Mujahedin Detachment and 4th and 3rd Manoeuvre Battalion. This is a regular operation, regular activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can I tender this document into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 438.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: This is a convenient time for the break, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And my learned -- Mr. Mundis has a short announcement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If I could, I didn't want to interrupt the flow earlier. I would suggest, again, as was the case last week with Operation Uragan, which we indicated means "hurricane," Proljece means "spring" in the Bosnian language, and I would respectfully ask if the interpreters could, in -- when we refer to that operation, too, again use the original "Proljece," since that's what the documents refer to, and it might avoid confusion later when we have "Operation Spring" or "Operation Proljece" in the transcript. So I would ask when we're referring to the military operations if we could retain their original Bosnian names since that's what will appear in the documents, it might avoid confusion many months from now when we're reviewing the transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It helps a great deal, but it adds to my confusion. A little earlier when I asked whether the Spring II and the Proljece 95 action was the same thing. And I was told no, Spring was in May and Proljece was in July. Now --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The actions were in May and July.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We can go back to that issue with the witness when we return, Your Honour. That -- there were references to Proljece and Proljece II, and we'll -- we'll clear that up with the witness after the -- after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We'll take the break and come back at half past 12.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I want you to clarify. In what month was Operation Proljece conducted? In what month of 1995?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Proljece was conducted in the month of May 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the objective of Proljece was, again?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: The objective of Proljece operation was to take up Podsjelovo ridge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in what month was Operation Proljece II conducted in 1995?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Proljece II was in the month of July 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was its objective?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: The objective of the operation was to capture the features of Krcevine, Gaj, and Malovan.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to go back to document PT2075, a document which I tried to show earlier which was not available. We see in the B/C/S it's from the 15th of May, 1995. I hope that the English translation is corresponding now. We had this earlier.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It says on the upper right-hand side in the addressee field: "Komandir 35th Division." Have you ever seen this document?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know whose handwriting this is?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what are you clarifying here with your handwriting?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: 02, that's the chief of staff. We had numbers assigned to each and every one of us. And I'm giving him an assignment and telling him what he has to do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what has the chief of staff to do?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: He has to implement these tasks that were mentioned herein.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who's giving these tasks?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: In order for the subordinate units to take -- to carry out their tasks, they have to have in their plans, among other things, these various requirements.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you look at the document 15th of May, 1995, to which combat operations does this relate to, this document?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Proljece.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not Proljece II, yeah? To clarify.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: No, Proljece, the 15th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I wish to tender this document into evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before you do that, I would like to see the "02" that is supposed to be the chief of staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can -- can the size of the B/C/S please be reduced. Thank you. Is it maybe possible for the witness to indicate where "02" is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Yes. And I want to be --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the President, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I would also like the rest of the handwritten stuff to be explained. I don't think -- unless all that -- that's written on it is supposed to be "02".

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I will endeavour to do so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you indicate where you marked "02" on this document.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: I -- I didn't. I marked it as "02".

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Where is the "02"?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you take the pen and encircle where the "02" is, please.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And mark a "1" next to it, please.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And what is that -- what does the rest of the writing mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm giving the assignment to the chiefs -- chief of staff, for him to carry it out as far as he can. And the tasks or assignments are contained therein.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The chief of staff of what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The chief of staff of the division.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Did I understand you to say that this document was authored by you, or -- or did I miss that? Who is -- whose signature is this at the bottom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't author the document. I received the document as part of the preparations for Proljece. This is the signature of the commander of the Mujahid detachment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And what is the name of the commander there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Abu Mali.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. And -- okay. And then you wrote by hand further instructions to other people. Do I understand that? Or to him again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To other people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. You answered to the question who was the chief of staff -- okay. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you state the name of the chief of staff, please.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Nedzad Sabic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 439.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. -- Mr. Neuner, either now or some point later before you complete your examination-in-chief, I would like you to go a little more into detail with your witness about the background of this document. Obviously, this is the first time we've seen anything in writing from any of the members of the El Mujahid Detachment, so it attracts some interest to me. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you see here a stamp next to the signature of Abu Maali. Can you explain to the Judges what this stamp is about.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: I don't know what you want me to say. This is a stamp as any other stamp of a unit. It's just as the next one. And this is the first time that I see it now here in this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I see a "1" below what looks to me like a weapon -- or the -- what is the symbol inside of this stamp?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: This seems to look like the coat of arms of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you explain the use in the "ABiH" of numbers within stamps. What does usually the number 1 stand for?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Stamps are produced in large quantities, and they each have their number. I don't see that it would have any other special meaning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does the number "1" mean, as opposed to number "2", for example?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: To my mind, it wouldn't really make any difference if the stamp had number "1" or number "2".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Why did Abu Maali on the 15th of May send this document?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: We said that this was part of preparations for Proljece operation, that they took part in this operation. Of all the units participating in this operation, I asked that they send me their proposals. And this unit, just as all the others, submitted their proposal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what are you doing with such proposals you get from Abu Maali or from other subordinated units?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: The division commander would make -- or rather, the division command would make an assessment, and as a result of that, they would either agree or disagree with proposals. The command would approve their plans or approve along with providing some small suggestions. Parts of these proposals would then become orders from the division. And then once the division commander had his order approved, combat activities would ensue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, again, you would seek approval from which level?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: From the level of the corps command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is obviously a plan of attack or proposal in writing. Were there also some meetings at the planning phase?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where would they take place?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Either at the place of deployment of the unit or it could be a subordinate unit or a division.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to move -- at these meetings, who attended?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Depending on the importance of the matters to be discussed at the meetings, you could have commanders, chiefs of staff, operations officers, assistants, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would this apply to the 35th Division or also to the units concerned?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The units also would submit proposals?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: The 35th Division, to the -- it applies to the 35th Division.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any meeting with members of the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: At the command post of the division. Shortly before combat, there were meetings in their place of deployment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to move back to the topic before the break. We talked about training. I have produced a map from the court binder in the meantime and want to distribute this briefly. In essence, we talked about the Cardak training centre or, you said at some point in time, the Ninth Kilometre. Could you indicate where the Ninth Kilometre or Cardak training centre you were referring to is on this map by encircling the location.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What have you just encircled?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: The Cardak area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you mark a "1" next to Cardak area, please.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the Ninth Kilometre, do you know where the Ninth Kilometre is?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Somewhere where the school building is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: [Marks] It's roughly here, but it's not marked on the map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Actually, you might have crossed the school building with the marking you just made. Maybe if I can --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No problem. We talked earlier about a document from the beginning of April where the -- where you talk about the Dvanaesti, the Twelfth Kilometre. You ordered that a base camp would be established. Could you indicate where the base camp you established in April is on this map.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: I only ordered that a base camp be set up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it set up?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: In what period of time?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe the order was from April 1995. 7th of April, 1995. Following that time period - it's former PT2016.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: The base was not set up at the Twelfth Kilometre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was it set up then?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: It was arbitrarily set up at the Thirteenth Kilometre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you mark where the Thirteenth Kilometre location is, where the camp indeed was set up.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: It is not plotted into the map. We have the Twelfth Kilometre, and further down by a kilometre it should be roughly -- well, it's difficult to show it on the map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you approximate where you believe the location was, the Thirteenth Kilometre you were referring to.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: I can't. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Just for the record, I was referring to a document from the 7th of April, 1995, Exhibit 434. If I could please ask that this map here is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The -- the map is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 440.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Finishing the training chapter, I want to show you a very brief video, PT number 0684. No audio needs to be played. The excerpt is starting at 7 minutes, 9 seconds and is runnings to 7 minutes, 47.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if possible could we hear the sound? Could we see -- hear the words uttered, if they are in a language we understand, of course?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Vidovic. I think I appreciate that too.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can the video portion which is about 30 seconds long please be shown again with audio this time. And, Mr. Hasanagic, I would ask you, if you know, to tell us whom you recognise and where you believe that location is.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We are playing the video again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you could tell us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is me there, the first one. Next to me is Ajman, the interpreter. This is me. I don't know this man.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We -- we had no interpretation. I don't know -- Madam Vidovic, did you understand what was being said?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry, we had no interpretation, so we don't --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: This is -- this is actually the reason -- we had problems to find the exact beginning of the text -- why I didn't play the audio in the fist place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Hasanagic, could you explain where you have been in this moment.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I believe that was at the Ninth Kilometre, at training.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were referring to a man next to you. Could you just state the name of this man for the record, please.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: That was the interpreter, Ajman. He was the sole person I communicated with, because he was the only one who spoke our language.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was of which unit?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: The El Mujahid Detachment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise anybody else?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: There was I. Next to me, Ajman. And next to him, the commander of the 329th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was his name?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Fehim Skulj [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can I please tender this excerpt into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We'll do that just now. Mr. Hasanagic, you said you had an interpreter sitting next to you. Did he interpret to you what that other gentleman was saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. The interpreter interpreted for the rest of the meeting. He spoke English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner, I apologise. I wish you would take the witness back to the -- to the video and explain a little more what -- what sort of meeting was this and -- and were there -- the other members -- I didn't see the other participants in the meeting, but -- but I understand that they were from other units or -- or -- you know, what was going on at the meeting. Could you --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could we maybe play the video again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And while it is being played could you explain what the Judges are interested in, or Judge Harhoff particularly. What is the purpose of this particular gathering?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I came to the barracks where training was conducted. The El Mujahid Detachment took part in the training. We sat down at a table and we made a brief analysis of what had been done there. In addition to me, there was the interpreter and the commander of the 329th, because his unit was attending the training at the time. And I believe that's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You -- you said you didn't know the man with the white cap and spectacles who was speaking. Do you know which unit he belonged to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I didn't at the time. Presumably, he was from the detachment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: When you say you didn't at the time, then you invite the question that says: Did you come to know later?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much. Are you done, Judge?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That clip is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 441.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said they were training at the time. For which of the many operations we were talking about earlier, for which operation was this training conducted, if you remember today?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: The training was conducted for Operation Proljece II and for the operation in September.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for this clarification. Who was training? Who was in charge of the training?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: The brigade commanders, the commanders of manoeuvre battalions and the commander of the El Mujahid unit were charged with conducting training.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And which manoeuvre battalions are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: 3rd, 4th, and 5th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I want to move, because you just mentioned the training was, among others, done for Proljece II, I want to move to this Operation Proljece II now and want to show you Exhibit 396. Have you ever seen this document?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who signed it?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: The commander of the 3rd Corps signed it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is happening here on the 2nd of June, 1995?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: The commander decided to re-subordinate the El Mujahedin Detachment again in the area of responsibility of the 35th Division for combat operation. He signed this order and by this order he regulated what the El Mujahid Detachment is supposed to do and accomplish within the area of responsibility of the 35th Division. It specifies here five tasks that they were supposed in cooperation and -- with the command of the 35th Division to accomplish.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see here on the second page of the English translation it talks about reconnaissance in three different places. Could you indicate in which part of the frontline these three places are lying.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: These are the features that the enemy used to shell Zavidovici and outlying villages, and these are the features of Blizna, Vis, and Paljenik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm sorry to interrupt, but if I may ask for the translation be corrected and the words in the Bosnian version "El Mujahedin" is referred to "El Mujahid" in this document, so it creates confusion throughout this trial. You can see for yourself: "The engagement of the El Mujahid Detachment," and it says in the English version "El Mujahedin." So we should use the correct term, the original term in translations from Bosnian into English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, you want the translation to be corrected in which document, ma'am? Just tell us the document you want corrected.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this document that we have on the screen --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes. What does it talk about?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It refers -- so in the title "Engagement of the El Mujahedin Detachment." Then under 3: "El Mujahedin" in item 3. And in the English version, instead of "El Mujahedin," what is used is "El Mujahid." What I'd like to ask, respectfully, is for the translation to faithfully reflect what is stated in the Bosnian original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We have taken a note of this and endeavour to have the translation service make a correction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Coming back to what we talked about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Maybe --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Maybe at one point you would wish to find out with the witness if, in his view, there were any difference between "Mujahid" and "Mujahedin," because I saw that in Abu Maali's combat plan, Abu Maali -- that we saw just a while ago -- Abu Maali himself seemed to call himself -- or his detachment "the El Mujahedin Detachment." So there is confusion about this point addressed by Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, being in the war theatre in 1995, could you shed some light on what my learned colleague from the Defence just raised, light on whether is there a distinction between "El Mujahid" and "El Mujahedin" Detachment or are we talking about one and the same group or unit?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: The full title of this detachment was the El Mujahedin Detachment. "Mujahid" is something else, but I could not explain in detail what it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you know what an El Mujahid is, as opposed to an El Mujahedin Detachment? And if you don't know, just say so.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would move on to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But let me -- let me just find out from the

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: these words were used like that? Did you -- in your mind, did you find them to be talking about one and the same unit or did they talk -- were they talking of different things?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know when this detachment was referred to that its name was El Mujahedin. Sometimes in conversation they would refer to a person within that as a Mujahid. I could not explain what that word "Mujahid" meant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have seen here in the document authored by Mr. Mahmuljin that he's talking about reconnaissance on the object of Paljenik. And in this regard, I want to show you document PT2151, a document which is eight days later, from the 10th of June, 1995. Do you recognise the document, is my first question.

utterances.speaker: At that time during the war, what was your understanding when
utterances.text: I do not see the signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we scroll down. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: At that time during the war, what was your understanding when
utterances.text: Yes. This is my signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In number 2, there is mentioning about reconnoitering, and there is also mentioning of Paljenik again.

utterances.speaker: At that time during the war, what was your understanding when
utterances.text: I transcribed the tasks that were handed down to the El Mujahedin Detachment by the corps commander, and here I order that in the area of my forces that were deployed there, that this detachment goes reconnoitering so that my forces would know that they should secure safe passage through their area and any other assistance, if they should need it. And -- but their tasks were handed down to me by the corps commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And for which operation are you ordering here the reconnoitering?

utterances.speaker: At that time during the war, what was your understanding when
utterances.text: That refers to the operation Proljece Dva, Proljece II.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I just go back to this question that Madam Vidovic raised a few minutes ago. Witness, you are saying in answer to your question now at page 58, starting at line 19: "I transcribed the tasks that were handed down to the El Mujahedin Detachment." In the document, on the B/C/S, it just -- I seem to see "El Mujahedin," without the word "detachment." If you look at that first line under that heading, "Naredjujem." Now, my question to you is: This detachment, did you refer to it as the "El Mujahedin Detachment"? According to your knowledge of it, is that how you knew it as?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the El Mujahedin. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You knew it as the -- did you -- what I'm trying to find out is: Did you also know it as a detachment, an El Mujahedin Detachment? Because you have used the -- at least, the English says here, when they translate your answer now, they've added the word "detachment."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is such a formation. The detachment of El Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, let me come up with the same objection to the translation. I'm not opposing this document, but if it says in the Bosnian version "El Mujahedin," let it be stated so in the English version. So this is the second document in a row that uses terminology which engenders confusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Indeed, madam, the document -- the document in English says "El Mujahid Detachment." But that's why I wanted to check with the witness whether he did actually say "El Mujahedin Detachment." Because that's what I have. When he speaks in Bosnian, I don't understand -- I don't hear that in the first place, and that's why I'm checking with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Maybe -- maybe, Your Honour, I can assist in this situation by asking a short question to the witness, because in the B/C/S it says: "Od." And then "El Mujahedin."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you explain what this "Od." stands for.

utterances.speaker: At that time during the war, what was your understanding when
utterances.text: That's abbreviation from "detachment." Sometimes we use the full word and sometimes the abbreviation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So could you for the record spell the word in Bosnian, the full word here abbreviated by "Od."

utterances.speaker: At that time during the war, what was your understanding when
utterances.text: "Od." means detachment, O-d-r-e-d.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: This being clarified, I hope to get Your Honours' permission to admit this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 442.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And I wish to move to the next document, which is PT2258.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question to you is: Do you recognise the signature?

utterances.speaker: At that time during the war, what was your understanding when
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whose signature is it?

utterances.speaker: At that time during the war, what was your understanding when
utterances.text: Mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to take you to the first line of this document which you're sending to the 3rd Corps command. You're stating here: "Pursuant to the order of the ARBiH General Staff and the order of the 3rd Corps command," and so on and so forth. Could you explain which two orders you have in mind when you were signing this document.

utterances.speaker: At that time during the war, what was your understanding when
utterances.text: I can't remember the order from the General Staff; neither the order from the corps command, but presumably they were connected. And my order ensued from those two orders, but I cannot remember those documents, but surely on the basis of those two documents I prepared this document, which is a report to the corps command. If I had those documents in possession now, this -- it would jog my memory most probably.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They are unfortunately not on my exhibit list for you, so I cannot show them to you. But I want to draw your attention to the last words of number 1. You're talking here about an approval of the 3rd Corps command.

utterances.speaker: At that time during the war, what was your understanding when
utterances.text: Yes, as I said, my order was approved by the corps command and, on the basis of that order, approved by the corps command, I embarked on accomplishing Proljece II operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: May I ask that this document be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I -- in this document and in other documents, I don't see the difference between the translation of "Mujahedin" and "Mujahid," but I would like all documents to use the terms as stated in Bosnian. In Bosnian, it's always stated "El Mujahedin," and then they are translated into "El Mujahid," and this causes confusion. Could you make sure that in all documents in your possession, could you check how this term was translated into English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, you say in this document you don't see the difference. I see the difference. It is still there if you look at paragraph 1, first line in the -- in the B/C/S, it's "El Mujahedin." If you look at paragraph 1, third line in the English, it's "El Mujahid Detachment." Now, having said that, let me say your -- your objection has been noted. Obviously these documents have now been translated and they're all going to come with this difference. We will remember you are -- what you noted. Okay? So what I'm trying to suggest to you: There's no need to -- to stand up each time you see it. We will -- you have made the point and that point is recorded. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Vidovic. Yes, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I think Your Honour Harhoff has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Yes. Because I would wish, before we leave this document - and I understood that you were just about to leave it and move on to the next document - that you go a bit into detail in interpreting the document. I hadn't seen the last part of the document, but in the part we have on the page, in number 1, if we go back to page 1 - thank you - it says that the witness is reporting back to the corps command that activities were carried out in coordinated action with the El Mujahid Detachment in keeping with the decision of the commander of the 35th Division. What do these words mean, "in coordinated action," "in keeping with the decision"?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you have heard the question. Could you please answer.

utterances.speaker: At that time during the war, what was your understanding when
utterances.text: Coordination -- "coordinated action" means that the decision was in coordinated action with the detachment in different occasions, and this is my decision previously approved by the corps command for the conduct of the Proljece II operation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I may ask an additional question to this point. Before, we had seen an order from the 2nd of June of 1995 re-subordinating the El Mujahedin Detachment to you, and now you're using the word "in coordinated action with." At this point in time, on the 18th of July, when you are writing this order, is the El Mujahedin Detachment still subordinated to you?

utterances.speaker: At that time during the war, what was your understanding when
utterances.text: Re-subordinated. Still re-subordinated to me, to us, and in coordinating action with my actions, that detachment conducted the Proljece II operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can this document please be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 443.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to move to PT2264, a document from the same day. Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: At that time during the war, what was your understanding when
utterances.text: Yes. This is the order for Proljece II operation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It says on the upper right-hand side: "Proljece 95 - II." And on the same page -- I withdraw my question.

utterances.speaker: At that time during the war, what was your understanding when
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you explain: On the same page, it also says "Proljece 95." But could you explain? This is a continuation?

utterances.speaker: At that time during the war, what was your understanding when
utterances.text: This is an activity conducted in July as a continuation of Proljece action against the features Krcevine, Gaj, and Malovan after the Podsjelovo feature had been captured from which they shelled Zavidovici and --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat the last part of the last sentence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you repeat the last part of your sentence. A feature had been captured from which they shelled Zavidovici, you said, and ...?

utterances.speaker: At that time during the war, what was your understanding when
utterances.text: The objective was to capture the elevations after Spring Operation after the Podsjelovo elevation had been captured. In Proljece II Operation, the objective was to capture the elevations of Malovan, Krcevine, and Gaj from which the enemy shelled Zavidovici as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Could you look at the last page.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you look at the last page, please. Whose signature is this?

utterances.speaker: At that time during the war, what was your understanding when
utterances.text: Mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were giving this signature, I'm interested whether you had an approval from somebody.

utterances.speaker: At that time during the war, what was your understanding when
utterances.text: I wrote my order and signed it on the basis of a proposal coming from the subordinated units, and such an order signed by me was forwarded to the corps commander. The corps commander approved the order with the map attached, sent it back to the division command, and then that was the point when I could start conducting combat activities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you get the approval from Mr. Mahmuljin before or after you signed this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner, the witness says: "I wrote my order and signed it on the basis of a proposal coming from the subordinated units, and such an order signed by me was forwarded to the corps commander."

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Then I'm confusing the witness. I withdraw my question. Can the document please be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 444.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to move to document 19 -- PT1921. Unfortunately, this document is cut into two; meaning, in two pages. Having just a look at the first page, could we go to the second page now. If we enlarge this. I'm interested in whose signature is this.

utterances.speaker: At that time during the war, what was your understanding when
utterances.text: It's my signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we go back to the first page again, please. It says here on the upper right-hand corner: "Proljece - 95-1." We heard Proljece --

utterances.speaker: At that time during the war, what was your understanding when
utterances.text: I think this is an error. It should have been "Proljece II." It's just a writing error.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: With this explanation, could I ask that the document be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 445.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Moving on to the next document, 2 -- PT2259. Could we -- have you seen this document?

utterances.speaker: At that time during the war, what was your understanding when
utterances.text: I think I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But could you explain what this type of document served for at the time.

utterances.speaker: At that time during the war, what was your understanding when
utterances.text: This is how we sent all documents to the units for the conduct of combat activities, and a similar document would go to the corps commander for the order form and for the schematic of the action on the map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So for sending out this document which is a list and the documents referred to here, at this point in time had you an approval of the 3rd Corps commander for sending such documents out?

utterances.speaker: At that time during the war, what was your understanding when
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I wish to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 446.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The next document is PT2236.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whose signature is this?

utterances.speaker: At that time during the war, what was your understanding when
utterances.text: Mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you explain -- I see from the translation it deals --

utterances.speaker: At that time during the war, what was your understanding when
utterances.text: I can't see what the date is. 28th of July. This is the -- the -- this is the interim combat report which speaks of the situation on the ground at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you look at number 2 of this document, we see a delivery of materiel from the 3rd Corps arrives, and it is dispatched to Livade. Could you explain what this means. Why is materiel dispatched to Livade?

utterances.speaker: At that time during the war, what was your understanding when
utterances.text: Elements of the El Mujahedin Detachment was deployed at Livade. The corps command sent down documents, and it was my duty to forward them on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I got the translation --

utterances.speaker: At that time during the war, what was your understanding when
utterances.text: Materiel, the materiel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. It's clarified now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can I ask that the document be tender into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 447.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to stay in the field of logistics and go to PT2247. We just talked about Livade. And my first question -- if we can scroll down the B/C/S. I'm looking for the signature. Whose signature is this?

utterances.speaker: At that time during the war, what was your understanding when
utterances.text: Mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you look at number 2 of your document, there is, again, Livade mentioned. Could you explain what was -- this is on the 16th of July, the document. What was happening in Livade then?

utterances.speaker: At that time during the war, what was your understanding when
utterances.text: A forward command post of the 35th Division was supposed to have been at Livade, because this is the only village in that area, along that axis, from where the Proljece II action could be easily commanded over.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And if you look at number 3, it talks about you, the commander of the 35th Division should be at the"KM." Could you explain what "KM" means and where that KM is in number 3.

utterances.speaker: At that time during the war, what was your understanding when
utterances.text: The command post for these activities was at grid point 777. This is higher ground, an elevation from which an attack was supposed to be launched. I was there; whereas, the -- the main command post was at Zavidovici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So we have a main command post, we have a command post at 777, and we have a forward command post at Livade.

utterances.speaker: At that time during the war, what was your understanding when
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In number 1, we see a KM in Malovan.

utterances.speaker: At that time during the war, what was your understanding when
utterances.text: Yes. This was along the axis of combat action and assignment of the El Mujahedin Detachment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would hand out a map to you, with the usher's assistance, and would ask you to show where 777 is, encircle it, mark a "1".

utterances.speaker: At that time during the war, what was your understanding when
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next to it, a "1", please.

utterances.speaker: At that time during the war, what was your understanding when
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you find Livade?

utterances.speaker: At that time during the war, what was your understanding when
utterances.text: You didn't tell me to look for it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: At that time during the war, what was your understanding when
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have encircled it. And please mark a "2" next to it.

utterances.speaker: At that time during the war, what was your understanding when
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then Malovan, please encircle it and mark a "3" next to it.

utterances.speaker: At that time during the war, what was your understanding when
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you stated -- we are talking about Proljece II. You stated earlier that one objective was Krcevine. Could you encircle "Krcevine" on this map.

utterances.speaker: At that time during the war, what was your understanding when
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And mark a "4" next to it.

utterances.speaker: At that time during the war, what was your understanding when
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe, when the attack occurred, where was -- from where to where was the main line or axis of attack?

utterances.speaker: At that time during the war, what was your understanding when
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you -- yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I wish to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just so that we are not confused later, could we also, on the other two lines, show the arrow, the direction of the arrow. You drew three lines there, but you -- you made an arrow on one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These are the two boundaries of the mission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. I beg your pardon. Thank you so much. Okay. The -- the map --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The map is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 448.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And I'm asking also that the document PT2247 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] PT2247 is admitted into evidence. May it also be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 449.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the judge, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to go to PT2271 now. If we can scroll down the B/C/S -- I think this is actually the old document, isn't it? Yeah. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise the signature?

utterances.speaker: At that time during the war, what was your understanding when
utterances.text: Yes. It's mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this is from the 20th of July at 9.00 in the evening, and it says: "Klek KM" in the header. Could you explain where Klek KM is.

utterances.speaker: At that time during the war, what was your understanding when
utterances.text: This is the other name for 777, triple 7. This is the entire area of Klek, and the grid point is 777. Some refer to it as "Klek KM" and others as "777 KM" but it's one and the same thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So at 9.00 on the 20th of July you're in Klek signing this document, or 777.

utterances.speaker: At that time during the war, what was your understanding when
utterances.text: Yes. This is shortly before the start of combat activities which ensued the following morning, and these were the assets, the materiel that I received from the corps command. Some of it was intended for the El Mujahid Detachment and some for the 328th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it mentions here a person Ajman in the village of Livade. Who is Ajman?

utterances.speaker: At that time during the war, what was your understanding when
utterances.text: Yes, that's the interpreter from the El Mujahedin Detachment. The only way I and my associates could keep in touch with that unit was through him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can I tender this document into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Yes, you can, Mr. Neuner. This document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 450.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I would try to get one or two documents -- I'm aware of the time -- in before the break. PT2285 is the next one.

utterances.text: Who signed this document?

utterances.speaker: At that time during the war, what was your understanding when

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you explain the materiel, technical equipment. What is the purpose of delivering it?

utterances.speaker: At that time during the war, what was your understanding when
utterances.text: This is Operation Proljece II we referred to a moment ago. This is the supplying of units with assets and materiel. It was sent down to me from the corps commander and it was my duty to forward it on to the forward command post at Livade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I wish to tender this document into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.text: I'm trying -- I have two more documents to finish this before the break. It's 2337, PT2337.

utterances.text: Who signed?

utterances.speaker: At that time during the war, what was your understanding when

utterances.text: And I ask you to look at number 2, where we -- where it mentions a shipment of materiel and supplies. Could you explain?

utterances.speaker: At that time during the war, what was your understanding when
utterances.text: Yes. The date is -- I can't make out what the date is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see better now?

utterances.speaker: At that time during the war, what was your understanding when
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. The 28th of July. The Operation Proljece II was still ongoing at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Neuner, it looks like now we are going to cause you to be -- not to be able to file the next document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER

utterances.text: The B/C/S says "28th of July." The English says "28th of February."

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes. We will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is -- are these one and the same document?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes, it is one in the same document. I see it is the same BROJ number. The translator actually made a question mark next to the "February." I think he was not sure. The witness just said it was the 27th of July.

utterances.text: Okay. 28th.

utterances.text: 28th of July. I apologise.

utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, by your leave, can this be double-checked, please, but I do think that this document was already admitted today as 447. Perhaps the Prosecutor should double-check that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you explain briefly why distinguishing armbands should be worn by the participants of the Spring 95 battle, as it says in the first line under "Order."

utterances.speaker: At that time during the war, what was your understanding when
utterances.text: Precisely, in order to distinguish between the units participating in Proljece II. This was the usual practice with all the actions we carried out for units to have distinctive armbands, and this is something that the adjacent units were informed of too, in order to be able to recognise other units. This was normal procedure carried out in combat. We also had -- these were distinctive signs. Whoever was in the area of -- in the combat area, the participating units would know who they're up against or who they've encountered.
